goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Adding the same host with a different category succeeds without uniqueness enforcement, but imports silently use the first row's category instead of the newly saved assignment.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: EmbeddableHost model has no uniqueness validation on the 'host' column (seen in app/models/embeddable_host.rb lines 1-24), and the record_for_host method uses `.first` (line 17) which would return an arbitrary record if duplicates exist. The migration also doesn't add a unique index. This means duplicate hosts can be created, and when looking up which category to use for embedding (in topic_embed.rb line 39: `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)`), it will use whichever record is returned first, potentially ignoring the user's intended category assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — Changing the enabled category chooser while a save is pending makes the success callback display the new selection although the server persisted the earlier category.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 29-38: The code captures `this.get('categoryId')` at line 33 before the async save, then in the success callback at line 36 it uses `this.get('categoryId')` again. If the user changes the category selection while the save is in flight, the callback will use the new categoryId value rather than the one that was actually sent to the server. This is a race condition where the UI could display a category that wasn't actually persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:762 — Removing `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` without a compatibility period breaks existing site-settings API clients and plugins that still read or write those keys.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows removal of `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` from config/site_settings.yml (lines 762-763 area). The migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb migrates data from these settings to the new EmbeddableHost model and then deletes them. While this is a valid architectural change, the finding raises a legitimate concern about external API clients or plugins that may depend on these settings. However, this is more of a backwards compatibility/deprecation concern rather than a bug - the code correctly migrates the data. It's an important architectural consideration but not a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/site_setting.rb:68 — Removing `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` without a compatibility shim breaks plugin callers at runtime after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` method is being removed from app/models/site_setting.rb (lines 71-84 are deleted). The functionality is being replaced by `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` in the new model. While this is a valid refactoring within the codebase (all internal callers are updated), the finding raises a legitimate concern about external plugins that may depend on this public API method. However, this is not a 'bug' per se - it's an API breaking change concern. The diff doesn't show any deprecation warning or compatibility shim being added. This is a real architectural/scope concern about backward compatibility for plugins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Hosts saved with an accepted port such as example.com:8080 never match URI.host and cannot embed comments.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. Looking at the diff, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` at line 10-17 extracts `uri.host` from the URL and compares it against the stored host. However, the `before_validation` callback strips the protocol and path but preserves the port (e.g., 'example.com:8080'). The validation regex at line 2 explicitly allows ports: `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`. So a host like 'example.com:8080' can be saved, but `URI('http://example.com:8080/page').host` returns just 'example.com' (without port), which won't match 'example.com:8080' in the database. This is a legitimate correctness bug where hosts with ports will never match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Limiting top-level domains to five characters rejects valid hosts such as example.technology and prevents their configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. This would reject valid modern TLDs like .technology, .photography, .international which have more than 5 characters. This is a real bug that prevents legitimate hosts from being configured.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — Saving with no selected category overwrites the server's uncategorized fallback with a lookup of null and displays an incorrect empty category.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 29-38, after saving, it calls `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. If categoryId is null/undefined (no category selected), this will set the category to null/undefined on the client side. However, the server-side code in embeddable_hosts_controller.rb lines 22-23 shows that when category_id is blank, it defaults to uncategorized_category_id. So the server saves with uncategorized, but the client displays null/empty because findById(null) returns nothing. This is a real UI inconsistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Default or unset `embed_category` produces no joined row, so `[0]['id']` aborts the migration before configured hosts are copied.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 10-14 show: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If 'embed_category' is not set or doesn't match any category name, the query returns no rows, and accessing `[0]['id']` on an empty result will raise an error (nil reference), causing the migration to fail before the fallback logic on lines 17-19 can execute. The fallback check `if category_id == 0` would never be reached because the error occurs first.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Raw-inserting legacy URL-form host entries skips normalization even though the old setting accepted them, causing those hosts to stop matching after the setting is deleted.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the migration. Looking at the migration code, it reads old `embeddable_hosts` values and inserts them directly into the new table without normalization. However, the old setting accepted URLs with 'http://' or 'https://' prefixes (as shown in the removed `allows_embeddable_host?` method in site_setting.rb which stripped these prefixes). The new `EmbeddableHost` model has a `before_validation` callback that strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes, but the migration uses raw SQL INSERT which bypasses model validations. This means if someone had 'http://example.com' in their old settings, it would be inserted as-is, but the new `host_allowed?` method compares against `uri.host` (just 'example.com'), causing a mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting both legacy settings inside `change` has no restorative rollback, so a rollback leaves old code without its embedding configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the migration uses `change` method but includes `DELETE FROM site_settings` statements at line 31. Rails migrations using `change` can auto-reverse certain operations like `create_table`, but raw SQL `execute` statements with DELETE cannot be automatically reversed. If this migration is rolled back, the `create_table` would be reversed (table dropped), but the deleted site_settings records would not be restored. This is a legitimate concern about migration reversibility - the migration should either use `up`/`down` methods with explicit restoration logic, or acknowledge it's irreversible. However, this is an architectural/design concern rather than a bug since the migration works correctly going forward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — saveChanges is an added action with no caller, leaving a dead update path to maintain.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims saveChanges has no caller and is dead code. However, looking at the diff, this is a new admin controller being added as part of a larger feature for embedding configuration. The saveChanges action is defined in the controller and would be called from the template (admin/templates/embedding.hbs). While the current template shown in the diff doesn't explicitly show a save button calling saveChanges, this is a new feature being built and the action is part of the controller's public interface. The finding incorrectly assumes this is dead code when it's actually part of a new feature's controller that may be called from templates or future UI additions. The diff shows this is initial scaffolding for an embedding admin feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Indexing the embed_category query result without handling an absent override row can crash the migration and block deployment on sites using the default setting.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, line 11 does `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If the embed_category site setting doesn't exist or doesn't match any category name, the query returns no rows, making `[0]` return nil, and `nil['id']` would raise a NoMethodError. The code does handle category_id == 0 on line 14-16 by falling back to uncategorized_category_id, but the crash happens before that check if the query returns empty results. This is a real bug that could crash migrations on sites that never set embed_category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — Update and delete dereference a nil record for stale or unknown IDs, turning routine admin races into HTTP 500 responses.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb, the update and destroy methods use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` which returns nil if the record doesn't exist. Then `save_host(host)` is called with nil in update, and `host.destroy` is called in destroy - both will raise NoMethodError on nil, causing HTTP 500 errors. This is a real bug where invalid/stale IDs cause unhandled exceptions instead of proper error responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — The delete request has no rejection handler, so a server or network failure becomes an unhandled promise with no error feedback to the administrator.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 46 in embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler for the promise. In contrast, the save action at line 38 properly handles errors with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. This is a real defect where network/server failures during delete operations will result in unhandled promise rejections with no user feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating stored host values without SQL quoting lets an apostrophe break the migration or injected SQL execute with migration privileges.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb line 25, the code does: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The variable `h` comes from user-stored data (embeddable_hosts site setting split by newlines) and is directly interpolated into the SQL string without any escaping or quoting. If a host value contains an apostrophe or malicious SQL, it could break the migration or allow SQL injection. This is a real security/correctness bug in the migration code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:6 — The new CRUD controller is covered only by an inheritance assertion, so create, update, delete, and validation-error behavior can regress undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new EmbeddableHostsController (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb) only has a single test checking inheritance ('it is a subclass of AdminController'). Looking at the diff, the controller in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb implements create, update, and destroy actions with actual business logic (save_host method with validation and error handling), but none of this functionality is tested. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:6 — The new embedding endpoint is covered only by an inheritance assertion, leaving host serialization and staff-only access untested.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb only contains an inheritance assertion (line 6: 'expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)'). The diff shows the controller has show and update actions that serialize embedding data with embeddable_hosts, but there are no tests for the actual endpoint behavior, serialization, or staff-only access verification. This is a legitimate test coverage concern for newly added functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — No test verifies that a new embedded topic receives the matched host's category, so administrator category assignments can regress silently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's no test verifying that a new embedded topic receives the matched host's category. However, looking at the diff in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb, lines 36-37 show: 'expect(post.topic.category).to eq(embeddable_host.category)' - this is exactly a test that verifies the embedded topic receives the matched host's category. The finding is factually incorrect.
